title: A torus in a parabolic extends to a geometrically maximal torus
statement: Let $k$ be any field [def-weil-field] and let $G$ be a reductive $k$-group [def-sc-group-scheme, def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]: smooth, affine of finite type and geometrically connected, with no nontrivial smooth connected normal unipotent subgroup after algebraic closure. Unipotent means that all geometric points are unipotent matrices in a faithful finite-dimensional representation. A parabolic $k$-subgroup $P\subseteq G$ is a smooth geometrically connected closed subgroup [def-weil-closed-immersion] such that the fppf right-coset sheaf $G/P$ is represented by a proper finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. This sheaf is the sheafification of $A\mapsto G(A)/P(A)$ for faithfully flat finitely presented coverings of commutative $k$-algebras, with $G(A)=\operatorname{Hom}_k(\operatorname{Spec}A,G)$. A torus is a group scheme becoming $\mathbf G_m^r$ over an algebraic closure, $r\geq0$, with $\mathbf G_m=\operatorname{Spec}k[z,z^{-1}]$ and multiplication of units. Let $P\subseteq G$ be parabolic and let $D\subseteq P$ be a closed torus, not necessarily split. There exists a closed torus $T\subseteq P$ containing $D$ such that $T_{\bar k}$ is maximal among closed tori in $G_{\bar k}$ for every algebraic closure $\bar k/k$. The trivial torus, $P=G$, finite fields and imperfect fields are allowed.

source.place: Theorem 17.82 and Corollary 17.83, printed p.379; Theorems 17.10 and 17.16, pp.354--356 (a parabolic contains a geometric Borel, so its maximal tori are maximal in G); Theorem 25.1, p.544, converse, choice of a maximal torus in P, with the prescribed contained torus retained.

proof.text: Among the closed tori of $P$ containing $D$, choose $T$ of greatest dimension. The collection is nonempty because it contains $D$. By [lem-sfb-multiplicative-type-largest-subtorus], every such torus is smooth and connected. By [lem-sfb-solvable-normal-subgroup-products], their dimensions are nonnegative integers bounded by $\dim P$, and a strict inclusion between smooth connected groups strictly increases dimension. Therefore no larger torus of $P$ contains $T$: $T$ is maximal in $P$. This argument retains the prescribed $D$, including when $D$ is trivial.

source.place: Corollary 17.83 and its proof, printed p.379; greatest-dimension choice with the given torus retained, as also used in Corollary 17.85, pp.379--380.

proof.text: Fix any algebraic closure $F/k$. The parabolic $P$ is smooth, connected, affine and of finite type by hypothesis (it is closed in the affine finite-type $G$). Apply [lem-sfb-maximal-torus-field-extension] to $(P,T,F/k)$: $T_F$ is maximal in $P_F$. Both $P_F$ and $G_F$ are smooth by [lem-pc-proper-base-change] and connected by the geometric-connectedness hypotheses; their affine coordinate algebras are finitely generated by the original generators after tensoring with $F$. Set $X=G/P$. By the proper-base-change clause of the same node, $X_F$ is proper, hence of finite type. For an $F$-algebra $A$, the functor-of-points identifications give $G_F(A)=G(A)$ and $P_F(A)=P(A)$. Every $A$-algebra used in fppf sheafification inherits its compatible $F$-structure. Thus the local coset descriptions of $X_F$ and $G_F/P_F$ coincide, so they represent the same quotient sheaf. This identification takes the image of $1$ to the identity coset.

source.place: Theorem 17.82 and Corollary 17.83, printed p.379; extension to an algebraic closure before applying Theorem 17.16, printed p.356.

proof.text: Choose a Borel $B$ of $G_F$ using [lem-sfb-borel-conjugation-cover]. Let it act by left multiplication on the nonempty proper finite-type scheme $X_F=G_F/P_F$ (the identity coset proves nonemptiness). Since $B$ is smooth, connected and solvable, [lem-sfb-solvable-proper-fixed-point] gives a point $x\in X_F(F)$ fixed by $B$ on every $F$-algebra. By [lem-sfb-homogeneous-orbit-quotient-geometry], lift $x$ to $g\in G_F(F)$. For every $F$-algebra $A$ and $b\in B(A)$, $bg_AP_F=g_AP_F$. The quotient-node isomorphism $G_F\times P_F\simeq G_F\times_{X_F}G_F$ implies $g_A^{-1}bg_A\in P_F(A)$. Hence the Borel $C=g^{-1}Bg$ is contained in $P_F$ scheme-theoretically. By [lem-sfb-borel-maximal-torus-conjugacy], $C$ contains a torus $S$ maximal in $G_F$. In particular $S\subseteq P_F$.

source.place: Theorem 17.16, converse proof, printed p.356; Theorem 17.10 and paragraph following Definition 17.12, printed pp.354--355.

proof.text: The torus $S$ is maximal in $P_F$, since a larger torus there would also be a larger torus in $G_F$. Now $S$ and $T_F$ are maximal tori of the smooth connected affine finite-type group $P_F$. Apply the conjugacy clause of [lem-sfb-borel-maximal-torus-conjugacy] to that group, without assuming it reductive: some $p\in P_F(F)$ satisfies $pSp^{-1}=T_F$ as subgroup schemes. If a torus $R\subseteq G_F$ contains $T_F$, then $p^{-1}Rp$ contains $S$, so maximality of $S$ forces $p^{-1}Rp=S$ and $R=T_F$. Therefore $T_F$ is maximal in $G_F$. The torus $T$ was chosen over $k$ before the arbitrary choice of $F$, so this proves the assertion for every algebraic closure with the same $D\subseteq T\subseteq P$.

source.place: Theorem 17.10, printed pp.354--355, applied inside P after Theorem 17.16; Theorem 17.82, printed p.379.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 17.82 and Corollary 17.83, p.379; Theorem 17.16, p.356; Theorem 17.10 and paragraph following Definition 17.12, pp.354--355. Prescribed containment is retained in the greatest-dimension choice.
